boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase, under-21-safe ways to spend time on or close to the Berkeley campus.

cards.entity_name: UC Berkeley Free Guided Walking Tours
cards.title: Take the free campus walking tour
cards.subtitle: Koret Visitor Center to Sproul Plaza
cards.notes: Reserve a spot, meet at the stated tour start, and use the 90-minute accessible walk to orient your group to campus landmarks.
cards.short_summary: A university-led, outdoor campus walk with student ambassadors.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley offers free 90-minute accessible walking tours seven days a week; registration is required.
cards.source_title: Free Guided Walking Tours | Visitor Services
cards.access_notes: Free tour; register in advance. Tours are outdoors and begin at Koret Visitor Center except on home football weekends.

cards.title: Ride up the Campanile with campus ID
cards.subtitle: Central UC Berkeley campus
cards.notes: Bring a current campus ID and check visitor operations before heading over; spend the visit taking in the tower’s views and carillon setting.
cards.short_summary: Campus-ID holders can visit Berkeley’s clock and bell tower without admission cost.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission to the Campanile is free for UC Berkeley students, faculty, and staff with campus ID.
cards.access_notes: Free only for UC Berkeley students, faculty, and staff with campus ID; other visitors pay admission.

cards.title: Walk the Botanical Garden
cards.subtitle: 200 Centennial Drive, Berkeley
cards.notes: Bring your current UCB ID, choose a daylight visit, and follow the garden’s path and visitor guidelines while exploring its living collections.
cards.short_summary: A 34-acre research garden with free entry for current Berkeley affiliates.
cards.evidence_claim: Current UC Berkeley students, faculty, and staff receive free Botanical Garden admission when they bring ID.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | UC Botanical Garden
cards.access_notes: Free for current UCB faculty, staff, and students with ID; reservations are recommended for other visitors and standard admission otherwise applies.

cards.entity_name: Berkeley Art Museum and Pacific Film Archive
cards.title: Browse BAMPFA on Free First Thursday
cards.subtitle: 2155 Center Street, downtown Berkeley
cards.notes: Plan for the first Thursday of the month, then enter the galleries and move through the exhibitions at your own pace with friends.
cards.short_summary: A monthly all-day free-gallery window at Berkeley’s art museum.
cards.evidence_claim: BAMPFA states that admission to its galleries is free all day on every First Thursday.
cards.access_notes: Free gallery admission is limited to First Thursdays; check the current event page before going. Film screenings are separately ticketed.

cards.title: See a show at Worth Ryder
cards.subtitle: 116 Anthropology & Art Practice Building, UC Berkeley
cards.notes: Check the exhibition calendar, then stop in during listed semester hours to view student-facing contemporary art exhibitions together.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery with public, no-admission exhibition access.
cards.evidence_claim: Worth Ryder Art Gallery is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Worth Ryder Art Gallery | UC Berkeley Art Practice
cards.access_notes: Free and public during listed fall and spring hours; the gallery is closed during summer and UC Berkeley academic holidays.

cards.title: Meet up in Doe Library
cards.subtitle: UC Berkeley campus
cards.notes: Use the public entrances to gather before a quiet reading break, then keep conversation low and follow posted library rules.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus library open to visitors without a pass or advance arrangement.
cards.evidence_claim: Doe Library is open to all researchers and visitors with no identification, registration, pass, or prior arrangements required.
cards.access_notes: Public access is free; consult current library hours before visiting and respect designated quiet spaces.

cards.title: Read and listen in Morrison Library
cards.subtitle: Doe Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Choose a book, magazine, or music listening break and settle in quietly; leave laptops behind because the room is laptop-free.
cards.short_summary: A public reading lounge inside Doe Library with books, music, and a deliberately quiet atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: Morrison Library is open to the public, and patrons may use many collections inside the room.
cards.access_notes: No admission is required; library borrowing needs a UC Berkeley library card. Laptops are not allowed in the room.

cards.entity_name: Valley Life Sciences Building Tyrannosaurus rex cast
cards.title: Find the VLSB T. rex cast
cards.subtitle: Valley Life Sciences Building atrium, UC Berkeley
cards.notes: Walk through the building’s public displays, pause at the towering cast in the atrium, and keep your visit clear of teaching spaces.
cards.short_summary: A public natural-history display anchored by a towering Tyrannosaurus rex cast.
cards.evidence_claim: UC Berkeley Library identifies public displays in Valley Life Sciences Building, including a towering Tyrannosaurus rex cast in the atrium.
cards.source_title: Places of pride: 10 LGBTQ+ landmarks to discover on the UC Berkeley campus
cards.access_notes: The cited campus source describes the building’s public displays; visit during normal building access and observe posted rules.

cards.title: Stroll the Berkeley Rose Garden
cards.subtitle: 1201 Euclid Avenue, Berkeley
cards.notes: Take the terraced paths slowly, pause at the pergola or overlook, and bring water for the uphill walk through the garden.
cards.short_summary: A terraced city rose garden with Bay views, public paths, and a pergola.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Berkeley states that entry to Berkeley Rose Garden Park is free.
cards.source_title: Berkeley Rose Garden Park | City of Berkeley
cards.access_notes: Entry is free. Listed hours are 6 AM–10 PM unless otherwise indicated; terraced paths can be steep.

cards.title: Spread out at Ohlone Park
cards.subtitle: 1701 Hearst Avenue, Berkeley
cards.notes: Meet on the five-block greenway for a low-key outdoor catch-up, then use the open areas and paths while leaving shared spaces tidy.
cards.short_summary: A long city green space near campus with paths, gardens, play areas, and recreation space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Berkeley describes Ohlone Park as a five-block stretch of green space with recreational activities, play areas, a community garden, and an off-leash dog area.
cards.access_notes: A public city park; no admission is listed. Use open areas respectfully and follow posted park rules.
